newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' 91-day T-bill rate at 10.617 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' 91-day T-bill rate at 10.617 pct.

text.p: Philippines' bellwether 91-day Treasury bill rate fell to 10.617 percent compared with last week's 10.822 percent, the Bureau of Treasury said on Tuesday.
The auction committee accepted only one billion pesos out of the 7.9 billion pesos worth of bids.
Average rates for 182-day and 364-day T-bills also went down due to oversubscription.
The six-month T-bills slid to 10.875 percent from last week's 11.475 percent, while the one-year bills slipped to 11.240 percent from 11.933 percent.
Bids for the six-month bills totalled 16.235 billion pesos, while tenders for the one-year bills were 12.429 bilion pesos.
The auction committe awarded only 1.5 billion pesos for the six-month bills and two billion pesos for the one-year bills.
"It seems we're on the way to normalcy, because the stock market is stabilising," Central Bank treasurer Sergio Edeza told Reuters after the auction.
Traders were expecting rates to decline due to the high liquidity in the system.
